Theorem
[continuously varying-set principle] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0056, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0057, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0058, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0059 ↗ lem:chow-ii-spatial-maximum-dini ↗ cor:chow-ii-dini-monotonicity 1. ch10:10.33\group Bundle maximum principles

If $\mathcal K(t)$ is a continuously varying family of closed, convex, parallel-invariant fibers and the ODE $U'=F(U)$ preserves it, then $u_t=\Delta u+F(u)$ preserves $\mathcal K(t)$.
Proof

\sketch Let $s(t)=\max _xd(u(x,t),\mathcal K_x(t))$. The distance is convex and its nearest-point support covector annihilates the Laplacian contribution by the second derivative test and parallel invariance. Comparing the ODE trajectory from the nearest point with $u$ gives $d^+s/dt\le Cs$. Since $s(0)=0$, the exponential barrier yields $s=0$.

□
